co_narrow_gauge_slabs.blurb: Narrow Gauge Slabs is a south-facing granite slab crag inside Pine Valley Ranch Park, southwest of Denver near the town of Pine. It is built for people new to leading: about fifteen routes, ten of them bolted and five on traditional gear, with grades running from very easy to 5.9. The climbing is friction and small edges on gently angled rock, with single pitches of roughly 70 to 100 feet and a handful of easier-topped multipitch lines. The sun exposure keeps it pleasant in cooler months, while summer is best saved for mornings. Good for families, guided groups and first lead attempts.
co_narrow_gauge_slabs.approach: From the park lots, follow the Narrow Gauge Trail downstream for roughly two-thirds of a mile to a signed spur that branches left to the base of the slabs.

co_jug_dome_aka_anne_s_rock.blurb: Jug Dome, also known as Anne's Rock, is a quiet sport crag on the north side of Big Thompson Canyon in the Estes Park valley. All fifteen routes are bolted, mostly between 5.7 and 5.10 with a single 5.11. The character swings between long slabs studded with large quartz crystals and short steep bulges that feel like gym climbing, and a few flakes are still loose because traffic has been light. The wall faces south and the approach is steep, cairned in places, and longer than first expected, so plan to work a little to get there.

co_main_warm_ups.blurb: Main Warm-Ups is a compact cluster of boulder problems among the roadside 7 Mile Boulders on Guanella Pass, near Georgetown. Fifteen problems fill the range from V1 up to the V6 level, with most landing between V1 and V4, so it suits a first session or a loosening-up circuit before heading to the harder boulders further along the trail. A short walk from the road brings you to the first boulder, and the rest sit just beyond it. High elevation keeps temperatures cool for bouldering.
co_main_warm_ups.approach: Walk back down the road a few minutes from the pullout, cross the bridge and look right for a signed trail, then follow it about five minutes to the first boulder.

_expect.name: Things Of Beauty (aka Interstate I-70 Towers)

co_things_of_beauty_aka_interstate_i_70_.blurb: Things of Beauty is a field of small, loose, dirt-like towers rising out of talus beside I-70 near Palisade, on the slopes of Mt. Garfield. Most of the fifteen routes are aid lines, nearly all at the gentle end of the aid scale, with a few free-climbing grades from 5.4 to 5.9 in the mix. The towers run from a few tens of feet to about a hundred feet tall. This is novelty climbing rather than quality rock, with real risk from poor protection, and it is appreciated as a winter outing for the photos and the oddity.

co_second_buttress_2.blurb: In Taylor Canyon outside Gunnison, Second Buttress is the big formation immediately north of First Buttress. Most of the fifteen routes here are traditional, with a few bolted lines, spanning 5.8 up to the low 5.13s but clustering around 5.10. Many are two or three pitches long. The rock is textured and sound, and the crack lines reward a standard rack. There are many more routes than the popular ones, particularly toward the right side of the wall, so there is room to explore beyond the classics.
